drug_class: Combination antidiabetic agent (long-acting insulin + GLP-1 receptor agonist)
purpose: This medication is used to help adults with type 2 diabetes control their blood sugar levels. It combines two different medicines in one injection to make managing your diabetes easier. It is typically used when diet, exercise, and other diabetes medicines are not keeping your blood sugar well controlled.
how_it_works: This medicine works in two ways at the same time. The insulin glargine part works like a background insulin that slowly lowers your blood sugar over 24 hours by helping sugar move from your blood into your body's cells. The lixisenatide part helps your body release more insulin after meals, slows down how fast food leaves your stomach, and tells your brain you feel full, all of which help prevent blood sugar spikes after eating.
common_side_effects: Low blood sugar (you may feel shaky, sweaty, dizzy, or confused), nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, upset stomach, headache, and reactions at the injection site such as redness or itching.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious low blood sugar, which can be dangerous — always have fast-acting sugar like juice or glucose tablets on hand. It has been associated with a risk of thyroid tumors in animals, so tell your doctor if you have a family history of thyroid cancer. Do not use this medicine if you have type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis. Tell your doctor about all your medicines since many drugs can affect blood sugar levels.
typical_dosing: This medicine is injected under the skin once a day, within one hour before your first meal of the day. Your doctor will start you on a dose based on your current insulin use and will slowly adjust it to find the right dose for you. It comes in a pre-filled pen device, and your healthcare team will show you exactly how to use it.
